discovery: Laser- and beam-driven plasma wakefield acceleration of particles

nominees.name: Chandrashekhar Joshi
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

motivation: In 1979 Tajima, with the late John Dawson, showed theoretically that an intense laser pulse in a plasma excites a wake wave whose electric fields exceed those of conventional accelerators by three orders of magnitude. Joshi turned plasma-based acceleration into experimental reality, from beat-wave acceleration to the beam-driven plasma wakefield experiments at SLAC that doubled the energy of 42 GeV electrons in under a metre. Malka and his team at LOA produced the first quasi-monoenergetic laser-plasma electron beams (2004) and demonstrated controlled injection and stable, tunable beams. Together they established a new physical principle for accelerating matter, using collective plasma oscillations, which now yields multi-GeV beams in centimetre-scale plasmas, compact X-ray sources and a credible route to future colliders. This work exemplifies plasma physics at its best: clear theory leading to measurable effects and to new tools for exploring matter under extreme conditions.
